content:
I am preparing materials for a research project on how people categorize everyday social
and economic situations. An earlier conversation produced four vignettes for a class of
"indignant responders", defined as follows:

CLASS B (indignant responder): the responder reads the other side's conduct as wrong —
one-sided terms, an exploitative arrangement, someone taking advantage — and responds by
refusing the terms or withholding everything, even at a real cost to themselves. The
point of the response is to condemn and punish the conduct, not to gain.

Here are the four current vignettes:

B1 (individual; proposed_terms): Yara, 45, needs to sell her late husband's boat quickly. Her brother-in-law Piet, who knows the marina crowd, offers to broker the sale — keeping ninety percent for his connections. Even a tenth would exceed what Yara could get alone before the storage fees hit. She refuses outright and lets the deadline pass, telling Piet she would rather absorb the loss than reward someone squeezing a widow.

B2 (individual; entrusted_proceeds): Hassan, 52, agreed to sell a sedan for his neighbor Roy, keeping a commission from the proceeds. After the sale, a mechanic friend shows Hassan proof the odometer was rolled back before Roy handed the car over. The money is sitting in Hassan's account. He refunds the buyer in full, forfeiting his own commission, and tells Roy exactly why he will see none of it.

B3 (firm; proposed_terms): Petra owns a corner café. A national distributor offers her a supply contract: exclusivity, prices adjustable at their sole discretion, penalties if she stocks anything local. The numbers would still beat her current costs. Petra tears up the offer at the sales rep's table and emails every café owner she knows describing the clauses, accepting higher costs herself to make the terms publicly radioactive.

B4 (firm; entrusted_proceeds): Nnamdi's repair shop resells refurbished appliances. A landlord dropped off a truckload of washers and stoves, to be sold with Nnamdi keeping a cut. Then a former tenant recognizes her stove: the landlord had cleared units mid-lease while tenants were away. Nnamdi halts the sales, returns every traceable item to the tenants, and sends the landlord nothing — losing his cut and a steady account to answer the seizure.

Two of them (B2 and B4) have a flaw: the misconduct they punish is aimed at a THIRD
PARTY (a deceived buyer; dispossessed tenants). For this project, the condemned conduct
must be aimed AT THE RESPONDER: the responder discovers that the very party whose
arrangement they are part of has treated THEM one-sidedly, deceptively, or
exploitatively, and withholds everything in protest, at a real cost to themselves.

Write REPLACEMENTS for B2 and B4 only, with responder-directed grievances:

- B2: an individual person as responder; the setting involves money or goods the other
  party entrusted, advanced, or handed over first, from which the responder was to keep
  or pass on a share.
- B4: a firm, shop, or business owner as responder; same kind of setting (entrusted or
  advanced resources), in a market context.

CONSTRAINTS (same as the original generation)

1. 50-80 words, third person, one named responder as protagonist and one clearly
   identified other party.
2. Do NOT use the words "fair", "unfair", "selfish", "generous", "greedy", "cooperate",
   "cooperation", "moral", "trust", "betray", or their derivatives: the class must be
   conveyed by what the responder does and weighs, not by naming it.
3. Do not mention experiments, studies, games, players, laboratories, or questionnaires.
4. Do not use the dollar amounts 6, 12, or 18, and do not use a tripling of any amount.
5. Do not reuse any of these names (already used in the project): Elena Malik Ruth Jun Aditya Beatriz Calvin Dalia Farah Gideon Hyejin Isaac Jocelyn Karim Leona Mateo Noura Omar Paloma Quentin Rina Stefan Talia Ugo Valerie Waleed Ximena Yusuf Zora Anders Bruna Chen Deepa Emil Fatima Gabriel Helena Idris Johanna Kwame Lidia Musa Noemi Pavel Rasha Soren Tamara Viktor Oskar Denny Marisol Aldo Ingrid Dmitri Lena Yara Piet Hassan Roy Petra Nnamdi Wendy Carol Bram Aiko Lorcan Sylvie Marco Priya Devi Tobias Colette.
6. Do not duplicate the scenarios of B1 and B3 above; vary resource, relationship, and
   setting.

OUTPUT FORMAT

Return a single JSON object, no other text:
{"replacements": [{"id": "B2", "class": "indignant", "character": "individual",
"setting": "entrusted_proceeds", "text": "<the vignette>"}, {"id": "B4", "class":
"indignant", "character": "firm", "setting": "entrusted_proceeds", "text": "<the
vignette>"}]}

{"replacements": [{"id": "B2", "class": "indignant", "character": "individual", "setting": "entrusted_proceeds", "text": "Odile, 41, spent two months selling her uncle Gustav's stamp albums at collectors' fairs, splitting proceeds evenly after he handed the collection over. Settling up, a dealer shows her the albums were already declared stolen on Gustav's insurance claim — she had been moving them so his settlement would stand, her name on every receipt. Odile turns the albums and every cent over to the insurer, keeps nothing, and tells Gustav he chose the wrong cover."}, {"id": "B4", "class": "indignant", "character": "firm", "setting": "entrusted_proceeds", "text": "Silas stocks his delicatessen with estate olive oil fronted by importer Corbin, selling at Corbin's set price and remitting proceeds minus a fifth. Midway through the season, Silas finds Corbin's own website offering identical bottles at nearly half that price: his shop existed as the overpriced front that made Corbin's 'direct discount' look like a bargain. Silas crates every remaining bottle back to the warehouse, refunds his buyers from the till, and closes the account, forfeiting his fifth."}]}
